reviews.title: Good Product - Manual Included and Online
reviews.review_text: I have the XVM279NAV model that does not include the CD/DVD player. My vehicle has a CD player so I really did not need that feature but I will say it would probably be handy to have it included which it is on some models. I have a 2015 Chevy Equinox that did not have a navigation system nor a back up system. Just so you will know, you can in fact add the optional back up camera too, as stated on the box. Although it does include a fold up guide, you may find the online guide more helpful. It does include the link for the online manual. This product does have bluetooth and handsfree calling. This is built in IGO navigation. It has a front USB port which is extremely handy. It's 200 WATTS of peak power. For me, it is mostly self explanatory but I am on the high tech save end. However, I don't think anyone would have any problem using this product. The 7 inch touch screen is easy to see and does not take up a lot of room in my vehicle. This product is very nice to have, especially when traveling. I am considering the back up add on because my car did not come with that feature. Great product.

reviews.title: Too many negative points
reviews.review_text: Pros: - I like the potentiometer volume button because I can raise, reduce or mute the volume quickly compared to simple +/- buttons where you have to locate in the midst of other buttons and press many times - I like the MicroSD card reader - Loads in 6 seconds which is reasonable - I like the design and the icons seem cool Cons: - The screen is too opaque thus hard to see(dimmed to the minimum already, when dimmed to the max, it's pitch black which is pointless), just little sunlight (it was cloudy) and I could hardly see anything on the screen, barely bright enough, see for yourself on pictures - The touchscreen almost doesn't work, I have to press very hard (I really mean it, almost punching it) so that it detects what I pressed, very annoying, I was unable to set beep,camera options because of that and the touchscreen calibration option is proof showing how bad the touchscreen is otherwise such option wouldn't be there in the first place - There were no sticker labels on the wires, it would have helped for faster connection - No music detail for bluetooth audio - The volume resets everytime the car is turned off - The screen auto switches to radio after 10 seconds and it's annoying - The dim button is annoying when you aren't used to it and should be in the settings - The play/pause button stays the same so if there's a silence during the music, it's hard to know if it's playing or paused, especially when it's a little bit slow to react - Doesn't fit well on some old car models, my car is a 2004 Honda Civic Hybrid and I had to remove the frame in order to make it fit due to screw holes not matching, thus there's a small gap around the receiver(See picture) - Volume options have very limited options(See picture) - Buttons like dial, phone call, hangup, volume option are not very structured and located in not needed places - Beware camera is optional, thus not included

reviews.title: It's a relatively simple receiver. ...
reviews.review_text: It's a relatively simple receiver. But it packs a lot of audio features with a touch screen. The controls take a bit of getting used to and the volume knob is really small so be careful if you have big fingers. Switching between functions isn't the easiest and the skip buttons are kind of behind the knob. But the screen is large for the space and reasonably responsive.

reviews.title: This car stereo/media receiver allo...
reviews.review_text: This car stereo/media receiver allows one to perform the basic, everyday activities in a car. It's possible to play music on the radio or by connecting with your phone. It also allows you to be safer with the hands free functions. It's not as responsive as I might like for driving - sometimes I have to push the screen more than once to get it to do what I want. But as an entry level stereo, it would cover my needs.
